canonical_name: Dilworth's primary arbitrary-poset finite-width theorem with checked zero-width extension
canonical_statement: For every partially ordered set P and natural number k, if every (k + 1)-element subset of P contains two distinct comparable elements and some k-element subset is an antichain, then P is the disjoint set sum of k chains. For positive k this is the literal primary statement; the total-Nat encoding includes a separately checked k = 0 extension.

source_selection.citation: R. P. Dilworth, A Decomposition Theorem for Partially Ordered Sets, Annals of Mathematics (2) 51(1), 161-166 (1950), DOI 10.2307/1969503
source_selection.relationship_to_catalog: This phase selects the primary theorem identified at intake rather than silently choosing the easier modern finite-poset equality exposed by the blocked external Lean candidate. Its positive-width restriction follows the printed statement; k = 0 is an explicit conservative extension.
source_selection.review_boundary: The positive-width statement and page-161 definitions are frozen. The historical range convention for k and approval of the checked zero-width extension remain open, as do original pages 163-166, the complete finite and transfinite proofs, correction and errata status, and an independent H0 review.

canonical_formal_target.statement_identity_policy: The semantic statement identity is statement_bundle_sha256 over the explicit root expression and all three explicit support-definition bodies. elaborated_expression_sha256 alone identifies only the root expression that references those supports.

domain_and_universes: At arbitrary universe u: alpha : Type u with PartialOrder alpha; k : Nat; arbitrary Set alpha witnesses and a Fin k-indexed family of Set alpha chains.
ordered_binders: some exact-k set is an antichain
hypotheses: For every s : Set alpha, if s is equivalent to Fin (k + 1), then s contains two distinct comparable elements.
There exists s : Set alpha equivalent to Fin k that is an antichain under <=.
conclusion: There exists C : Fin k -> Set alpha such that every C i is a chain and every carrier element belongs to exactly one C i.

encoding_decisions.exact_finite_cardinality: HasExactly k s is Nonempty (s equiv Fin k), avoiding any collapse of infinite cardinalities to Nat zero.
encoding_decisions.dependent: The page-161 definition is encoded directly as existence of distinct comparable elements.
encoding_decisions.independent: The page-161 definition is encoded by mathlib IsAntichain for the partial-order relation <=.
encoding_decisions.chain: The page-161 pairwise-comparability definition is encoded by mathlib IsChain for <=.
encoding_decisions.disjoint_set_sum: A Fin k-indexed chain family with unique membership for every carrier element simultaneously states cover and pairwise disjointness.
encoding_decisions.empty_parts: The encoding does not separately ban empty indexed chains. For k > 0, the exact-k antichain lower bound and k-chain decomposition make every index necessary; k = 0 is handled explicitly.
encoding_decisions.boundary: The total-Nat target includes the empty carrier at k = 0 as a checked conservative extension and the singleton carrier at k = 1. The printed source does not explicitly resolve whether k ranges over zero, so source approval of this boundary remains open. No Finite carrier hypothesis is added.

minimal_import_result: The canonical-target fixture elaborates with the sole direct import and fails when it is removed. No Dilworth theorem or proof-bearing decomposition module is imported. Minimality is necessity of the declared import for this source layout, not an exhaustive comparison with every possible refactoring of mathlib modules.

checked_alternate_encodings.boundary: Only the local chain-decomposition predicate is expanded. No transport to the modern finite-poset minimum-partition equals maximum-antichain equality is credited.

uncredited_alternate_encodings: the modern finite-poset minimum chain partition equals maximum antichain equality
